'''Karakuni Shrine''' (辛国神社, からくにじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Fujiidera|en|Fujiidera|qid=Q634011|lt=Fujidera City|1=Fujiidera}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Murasya|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}.

== History ==
The name "Karakuni" derives from a branch of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|Mononobe clan|qid=Q1755836|lt=Mononobe clan|1=Mononobe clan}} that once ruled this area and produced the shamanistic figure {{ill|Karakuni Renzu|ja|辛国連|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karakuni Renzu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}—a disciple of {{ill|En no Gyōja|en|En no Gyōja|qid=Q198946|lt=Yaku Kogumi|1=En no Gyōja}}. Although the founding date is unknown, according to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}} in the entry for the 13th year, March of the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|en|Emperor Yūryaku|qid=Q357235|lt=Yuryaku Tennō|1=Emperor Yūryaku}}, it states that "Eka Chōno-mura was granted to Mononobe Ōren," indicating that the Mononobe clan, upon receiving these lands, enshrined their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|lt=Nigihayahi|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|1=Nigihayahi|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}, from which Karakuni Renzu later assumed responsibility for the rites.<ref name="藤井寺1">{{Cite book|lang=ja|title=Fujidera City History|volume=Volume 1, General History, page 638|date=1997}}</ref> According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}, on September 26 of the 9th year of {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan|1=Zhenguan}} ({{ill|867|en|867|qid=Q30347|lt=867 AD|1=867}}), the shrine was listed among the government-supported shrines, and it is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} as a government-issued small shrine. It appears that during this period the shrine was located to the southwest of 【Emisaka】.<ref name="ミナカワ1">[http://travel-minakawa.com/2018/01/01/post-917/ Southern Kawachi’s most beautiful and long approach – Introduction to Karakuni Shrine ~ Fujidera City ~] (Accessed May 21, 2022)</ref>
In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, the shrine was renamed "Karakuni Shrine" and, in {{ill|1872|en|1872|qid=Q7753|lt=1872 AD|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), it was designated as a {{ill|Murasya|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}. In {{ill|1907|en|1907|qid=Q2048|lt=1907 AD|1=1907}} (Meiji 40), the village shrine of Nonaka in Nonaka Village was merged, and the following year, the village shrine of Nagano in Fujidera (from the Nagano area) housed in {{ill|Fujii-dera|en|Fujii-dera|qid=Q6406788|lt=Fujii-dera|1=Fujii-dera}} was merged. As a result, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞鳴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} of Nagano Shrine was also enshrined.<ref name="藤井寺1">{{Cite book|lang=ja|title=Fujidera City History|volume=Volume 1, General History, page 638|date=1997}}</ref><ref name="ミナカワ1">[http://travel-minakawa.com/2018/01/01/post-917/ Southern Kawachi’s most beautiful and long approach – Introduction to Karakuni Shrine ~ Fujidera City ~] (Accessed May 21, 2022)</ref> Subsequently, Nonaka Shrine was re-established atop the posterior circular part of Nonaka Miyashiro Kofun in {{ill|1950|en|1950|qid=Q18597|lt=1950 AD|1=1950}} (Showa 25).
== Shrine facilities ==
[[File:Karakuni-jinja, Kasuga-inari-jinja.jpg|thumb|200px|Kasuga Inari Shrine]]
[[File:Karakuni-jinja, Kasuga-tenmangu.jpg|thumb|200px|Kasuga Tenmangu]]
Within the shrine grounds, there is a long approach (参道) covered in deep green foliage, which was selected in {{ill|1989|en|1989|qid=Q2425|lt=1989 AD|1=1989}} (the first year of {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}}) as one of the {{ill|Osaka Midori no Hyakusen|ja|100 Greens of Ōsaka|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Midori no Hyakusen|1=Ōsaka Midori no Hyakusen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11439936}}.<ref name="観光1">[http://www.fujiidera-kanko.info/spot/karakuni.html Karakuni Shrine – Fujidera City Tourism Association] (Accessed January 30, 2018)</ref> Additionally, along the approach there is a torii bearing the inscription "Nagano Shrine," which was relocated from Nagano Shrine.<ref name="藤井寺2">「Fujidera City History」, Volume 1, General History, page 635 (1997)</ref>
* Main Hall
* Haiden (worship hall)
* Kasuga {{ill|Tenmangū|en|Tenmangū|qid=Q798838|lt=Tenmangu|1=Tenmangū}} – enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}
* Kasuga {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|qid=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine|1=Inari shrine}} – enshrines {{ill|Ukano Mitama-no-Ōkami|ja|宇迦之御魂大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukano Mitama-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ|1=Ukanomitama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080728}}
* Administrative Office
* A remote worship area for {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingū|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}
== Festivals ==
* New Year's Festival ({{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1|1=January 1}})
* Setsubun Festival (on {{ill|Setsubun|en|Setsubun|qid=Q746798|lt=Setsubun|1=Setsubun}})
* Spring Inari Festival (on the vernal equinox)
* Great Purification Ritual of Mizu-nazuki ({{ill|June 30|en|June 30|qid=Q2657|lt=June 30|1=June 30}})
* Summer Festival ({{ill|July 17|en|July 17|qid=Q2729|lt=July 17|1=July 17}})
* Special Festival ({{ill|October 17|en|October 17|qid=Q2962|lt=October 17|1=October 17}})
* Monthly Festival (on the 1st day of every month)
